title: Config-declared template role and anchor bindings
description:
Replace the hardcoded template role and anchor names with repository-configured bindings so the template engine honors INV-DOMAIN-AGNOSTIC end to end.

## Background

The engine's node types are fully config-driven, but three names are compiled in and reached for by name: `PLANNING_ROLE` and `BREAKDOWN_ROLE` (`templates.rs:546,560`, consumed by breakdown, forced refresh, and validation) and the `container` anchor auto-bound from the positional CLI argument (`main.rs:2726`). A template using different role names silently falls outside the bracket tooling. Decision fixed at epic creation: the bindings become configuration (e.g. a `[templates.roles]` table) with defaults preserving the current names.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: The role names consumed by breakdown, refresh, and validation, and the auto-bound anchor name, are read from repository configuration; absent config yields today's names, so existing repositories work unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-2: A repository configured with different role and anchor names completes the full bracket flow (apply, breakdown, forced refresh) end to end, verified by an integration test.
- [hard] REQ-3: No role or anchor name literal remains in non-test engine code.
- [hard] REQ-4: The configuration reference documents the new keys, their defaults, and what each binding controls.

## Notes

Keep the binding lookup in one place (the template registry or config layer), so consuming commands ask for "the breakdown role" rather than re-reading config keys.
